3.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed modern Bibles, e.g. "I Am Who I Am" in v14 and "ancestors" for fathers), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, and no sentence over 14 words (sentence-length pass 2026-11-23). V14 keeps the KJV's I AM THAT I AM. V22 explains borrow as (ask), the meaning of the Hebrew word.

verses.text: Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law. Jethro was the priest of Midian. And Moses led the flock to the backside of the desert. He came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.

And the angel of the LORD appeared to Moses in a flame of fire. The fire was out of the middle of a bush. And Moses looked, and look, the bush burned with fire. And the bush was not consumed (burned up).
And Moses said: I will now turn aside, and see this great sight. I will see why the bush is not burnt.
And the LORD saw that Moses turned aside to see. Then God called to Moses out of the middle of the bush. God said: Moses, Moses. And Moses said: Here am I.
And God said: Do not draw near here. Put off your shoes from off your feet. For the place on which you stand is holy ground.
Moreover (also) God said: I am the God of your father. I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. And Moses hid his face. For Moses was afraid to look upon God.

And the LORD said: I have surely seen the affliction (suffering) of My people which are in Egypt. I have heard their cry by reason of (because of) their taskmasters (slave bosses). For I know their sorrows.

And I am come down to deliver (rescue) them from the Egyptians' hand. I will bring them up out of that land. I will bring them to a good land and a large. It is a land flowing with milk and honey. It is the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites. It is the place of the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
Now therefore, look, the cry of the children of Israel is come to Me. I have also seen the oppression (cruel treatment) of the Egyptians. I have seen how they oppress (treat cruelly) them.
Come now therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh. So you may bring forth (out) My people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
And Moses said to God: Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh? Who am I, to bring forth (out) the children of Israel out of Egypt?

And God said: Certainly I will be with you. And this shall be a token (sign) to you, that I have sent you. You will bring forth (out) the people out of Egypt. Then you shall serve God upon this mountain.

And Moses said to God: Look, I will come to the children of Israel. I shall say to them: The God of your fathers has sent me to you. And they shall say to me: What is His name? What shall I say to them?
And God said to Moses: I AM THAT I AM. And God said: This is what you shall say to the children of Israel: I AM has sent me to you.

And God said moreover (also) to Moses: This is what you shall say to the children of Israel: The LORD God of your fathers has sent me to you. He is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. This is My name for ever. This is My memorial (the way I am remembered) to all generations.

Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say to them: The LORD God of your fathers appeared to me. He is the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob. He said: I have surely visited (looked after) you. I have seen what is done to you in Egypt.

And I have said: I will bring you up out of the affliction (suffering) of Egypt. I will bring you to the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, and Amorites. It is also the land of the Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land flowing with milk and honey.

And they shall hearken (listen) to your voice. You and the elders of Israel shall come to the king of Egypt. You shall say to him: The LORD God of the Hebrews has met with us. Now let us go, we beseech (beg) you, 3 days' journey into the wilderness (desert). Then we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.
And I am sure that the king of Egypt will not let you go. No, he will not, not by a mighty hand.
And I will stretch out My hand, and smite (strike) Egypt with all My wonders. I will do them in the middle of it. And after that Pharaoh will let you go.
And I will give this people favour in the sight of the Egyptians. And it shall come to pass that you shall not go empty.

But every woman shall borrow (ask) of her neighbour. She shall ask of the woman who sojourns (stays) in her house. She shall ask for jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment (clothing). And you shall put them upon your sons, and upon your daughters. And you shall spoil (take the riches of) the Egyptians.

14.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that added things the KJV does not say, e.g. the angel 'usually in front' in v19 and 'that is how God drowned the Egyptians' in v27), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, and no sentence over 14 words (sentence-length pass 2026-11-23). V13 keeps the KJV's see the salvation of the LORD.

verses.text: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:

Speak to the children of Israel, that they turn and encamp (set up camp) before Pihahiroth. It is between Migdol and the sea, over against (across from) Baalzephon. You shall encamp (set up camp) before it by the sea.
For Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel: They are entangled (lost) in the land. The wilderness (desert) has shut them in.

And I will harden Pharaoh's heart (make Pharaoh stubborn), so that he shall follow after them. And I will be honoured upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host (army). Then the Egyptians may know that I am the LORD. And the children of Israel did so.

And it was told the king of Egypt that the people fled. And the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was turned against the people. They said: Why have we done this? We have let Israel go from serving us.
And Pharaoh made ready his chariot, and took his people with him.
And Pharaoh took 600 chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt. And he took captains over every one of them.

And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt (made him stubborn). And Pharaoh pursued (chased) after the children of Israel. And the children of Israel went out with an high hand (boldly).

But the Egyptians pursued (chased) after them, all the horses and chariots of Pharaoh. His horsemen and his army chased them too. And they overtook (caught up with) them camping by the sea. It was beside Pihahiroth, before Baalzephon.

And Pharaoh drew nigh (came near). Then the children of Israel lifted up their eyes. And look, the Egyptians marched after them. And they were sore (very) afraid. And the children of Israel cried out to the LORD.

And they said to Moses: Were there no graves in Egypt? Have you taken us away to die in the wilderness (desert)? Wherefore (why) have you dealt thus (done this) with us? Why did you carry us forth (out) out of Egypt?

Is not this the word that we did tell you in Egypt? We said: Let us alone, so that we may serve the Egyptians. For it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians. It was better than to die in the wilderness (desert).

And Moses said to the people: Fear not. Stand still, and see the salvation (saving power) of the LORD. He will show it to you to day (today). For you have seen the Egyptians to day (today). But you shall see them again no more for ever.
The LORD shall fight for you, and you shall hold your peace (stay quiet).
And the LORD said to Moses: Wherefore (why) do you cry to Me? Speak to the children of Israel, that they go forward.
But lift up your rod (staff). Stretch out your hand over the sea, and divide it. And the children of Israel shall go on dry ground through the sea.

And I, look, I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians (make them stubborn). And they shall follow them. And I will get Me honour upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host (army). I will get Me honour upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.
And the Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD. It will be when I have gotten Me honour upon Pharaoh. I will get honour upon his chariots and his horsemen.
And the angel of God went before the camp of Israel. He removed (moved) and went behind them. And the pillar (tall column) of the cloud went from before their face. It stood behind them.

And the cloud came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. It was a cloud and darkness to the Egyptians. But it gave light by night to Israel. So the one came not near the other all the night.
And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. And the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind. It blew all that night. He made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
And the children of Israel went into the sea upon the dry ground. And the waters were a wall to them. They were on their right hand, and on their left.
And the Egyptians pursued (chased), and went in after them into the sea. All Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his horsemen went in.

And it came to pass in the morning watch (early morning). The LORD looked to the host (army) of the Egyptians. He looked through the pillar (tall column) of fire and of the cloud. And He troubled the host (army) of the Egyptians,

And took off their chariot wheels, so that they drove them heavily (with great trouble). So the Egyptians said: Let us flee (run away) from the face of Israel. For the LORD fights for them against the Egyptians.
And the LORD said to Moses: Stretch out your hand over the sea. Then the waters may come again upon the Egyptians. They will cover their chariots and their horsemen.

And Moses stretched forth (out) his hand over the sea. And the sea returned to its strength when the morning appeared. And the Egyptians fled (ran) against it. And the LORD overthrew the Egyptians in the middle of the sea.
And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen. They covered all the host (army) of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them. There remained not so much as one of them.
But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the sea. And the waters were a wall to them. They were on their right hand, and on their left.
Thus the LORD saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians. And Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.
And Israel saw that great work which the LORD did upon the Egyptians. And the people feared the LORD, and believed the LORD, and His servant Moses.

8.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that added things the KJV does not say, e.g. rotting frogs shoveled into piles in v14 and Egyptians worshipping cattle in v26, and changed lice to gnats), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, and no sentence over 14 words (sentence-length pass 2026-11-23). V16-18 keep the KJV's lice. V26 keeps the KJV's abomination of the Egyptians.

verses.text: And the LORD spoke to Moses: Go to Pharaoh, and say to him: This is what the LORD says: Let My people go, so that they may serve Me.
And you may refuse to let them go. Then look, I will smite (strike) all your borders (land) with frogs.

And the river shall bring forth (out) frogs abundantly (in great numbers). The frogs shall come into your house, and into your bedchamber (bedroom). They shall come upon your bed, and into the house of your servants. They shall come upon your people, and into your ovens. They shall come into your kneadingtroughs (bread bowls).
And the frogs shall come up on you, and upon your people. They shall come upon all your servants.

And the LORD spoke to Moses: Say to Aaron: Stretch forth (out) your hand with your rod (staff). Stretch it over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds. Cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt.
And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt. And the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.
And the magicians did so with their enchantments (secret magic). They brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.

Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said: Intreat (pray to) the LORD, that He may take away the frogs. Let Him take them from me, and from my people. And I will let the people go to do sacrifice to the LORD.

And Moses said to Pharaoh: Glory over me (you choose the time). When shall I intreat (pray) for you, and for your servants, and for your people? Then the frogs will be destroyed from you and your houses. They will remain in the river only.
And Pharaoh said: To morrow (tomorrow). And Moses said: Be it according to your word. Then you may know that there is none like the LORD our God.
And the frogs shall depart (go away) from you, and from your houses. They shall depart from your servants, and from your people. They shall remain in the river only.
And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh. And Moses cried to the LORD because of the frogs. They were the frogs which the LORD had brought against Pharaoh.
And the LORD did according to the word of Moses. And the frogs died out of the houses, the villages, and the fields.
And they gathered the frogs together upon heaps (in piles). And the land stank.
But Pharaoh saw that there was respite (a break). Then he hardened his heart (made himself stubborn). He hearkened (listened) not to them, as the LORD had said.
And the LORD said to Moses: Say to Aaron: Stretch out your rod (staff), and smite (strike) the dust of the land. Then it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.

And they did so. For Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod (staff). He smote (struck) the dust of the earth. And it became lice in man, and in beast (animal). All the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
And the magicians did so with their enchantments (secret magic) to bring forth (out) lice. But they could not. So there were lice upon man, and upon beast (animal).
Then the magicians said to Pharaoh: This is the finger of God (the power of God). And Pharaoh's heart was hardened (stubborn). He hearkened (listened) not to them, as the LORD had said.

And the LORD said to Moses: Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh. Lo (look), he comes forth (out) to the water. And say to him: This is what the LORD says: Let My people go, so that they may serve Me.

Else (otherwise), you may not let My people go. Then look, I will send swarms of flies. I will send them upon you, and upon your servants and your people. I will send them into your houses. And the houses of the Egyptians shall be full of swarms of flies. The ground on which they are shall also be full.
And in that day I will sever (set apart) the land of Goshen. My people dwell (live) there. No swarms of flies shall be there. Then you may know this: I am the LORD in the middle of the earth.
And I will put a division (difference) between My people and your people. To morrow (tomorrow) this sign shall be.

And the LORD did so. And there came a grievous (very heavy) swarm of flies into the house of Pharaoh. They came into his servants' houses, and into all the land of Egypt. The land was corrupted (ruined) by reason of (because of) the swarm of flies.
And Pharaoh called for Moses and for Aaron, and said: Go, sacrifice to your God in the land.

And Moses said: It is not meet (right) to do so. For we shall sacrifice the abomination (a thing hated) of the Egyptians to the LORD our God. Lo (look), shall we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes? Will they not stone us?
We will go 3 days' journey into the wilderness (desert). We will sacrifice to the LORD our God, as He shall command us.
And Pharaoh said: I will let you go to sacrifice to the LORD your God. Do it in the wilderness (desert). Only you shall not go very far away. Intreat (pray) for me.

And Moses said: Look, I go out from you, and I will intreat (pray to) the LORD. Then the swarms of flies may depart (go away) to morrow (tomorrow). They will depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people. But let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully (lie) any more. Let him not refuse to let the people go to sacrifice to the LORD.
And Moses went out from Pharaoh, and intreated (prayed to) the LORD.
And the LORD did according to the word of Moses. And the LORD removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh. He removed them from his servants and his people. There remained not one.
And Pharaoh hardened his heart (made himself stubborn) at this time also. Neither would he let the people go.
